rule: Never judge a visual change by reasoning about the code. Run `npm run shots` and LOOK at docs/shots/<label>/, comparing against docs/shots/00-baseline/. Never ask the user what something looks like.
reason: This project exists as a web port for exactly one reason: in the Godot original the agent could not see rendered output, so every art pass round-tripped through a human reviewer and the visual bar in sprite_style_guide.md was never met. The harness removes that bottleneck. Reintroducing the human-as-eyeball loop wastes the entire reason the port exists.
triggering_incident: sprite_style_guide.md line 207 states outright: 'The developer (user) serves as the visual reviewer since the AI cannot see the rendered result.' Milestone 1 of BRIEF.md was built specifically to retire that sentence.
enforced_by: npm run shots (byte-identical across runs; any pixel diff vs baseline is a real change)
retrieval_hints: how do I check what the game looks like
